result: The study used ChEC-seq with deep sequencing (12 combined samples, 650× coverage) to identify Mcm binding sites genome-wide with signal intensities varying over three orders of magnitude. The measurements showed high reproducibility (r² = 0.98-0.99).
evaluation: All three reviewers accepted the technical approach and data quality without criticism. Reviewer 1 stated 'the results are convincing,' and Reviewer 2 noted the authors 'combined the results of 12 independent assays to gain exceptionally deep coverage,' affirming the methodological rigor.

result: High-abundance CMBSs (ranks ≤500) were found within 100 base pairs of 82% of known origins in SGD and 78% of defined ACSs, leading to the conclusion that the vast majority of known origins are associated with the 500 most abundant CMBSs.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this validation of the method against known origins without objection. Reviewer 2 noted that the authors 'show that the location of Mcm2-7 location after loading are highly similar in the top 500 binding sites,' implicitly accepting this correspondence.

result: Analysis of published ssDNA data revealed replication initiation among the most abundant 1600 CMBSs, with peaks of ssDNA signal extending to the eighth cohort (ranks 1401-1600) and a rapid drop after the second cohort, demonstrating that replication activity parallels Mcm abundance.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 identified a critical weakness: 'the group-based (as opposed to analyzing individual Mcm2-7 binding sites) nature of the analysis prevents the authors from concluding that all of the 1,600 sites mentioned in the title act as origins.' This indicates the evidence supports replication at some but not necessarily all 1600 sites.

result: The most abundant 5000 CMBSs are located in intergenic nucleosome-free regions flanked by well-positioned nucleosomes, while CMBSs ranking >5000 largely correspond to nucleosomes. CMBSs remained intergenic until approximately rank 5000, then switched abruptly to genic localization.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these nucleosome positioning findings. Reviewer 1 noted the sites 'for the most part are free of nucleosomes,' and Reviewer 2 stated 'they find that there is a propensity of at least a subset of these sites to be nucleosome depleted,' affirming the nucleosome analysis.

result: The most abundant 5500 CMBSs are enriched for flanking ACSs approximately 35 base pairs from the Mcm binding midpoint, oriented consistently with in vitro Mcm loading by Orc. The degree of ACS match decreases with increasing rank, largely disappearing by rank 6000.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the ACS enrichment findings. Reviewer 1 stated the sites have 'characteristics consistent with origins of DNA replication, including the presence of ARS consensus sequences,' and Reviewer 2 noted 'at least a partial match to the ACS sequence,' affirming this analysis.

result: Mcm is typically loaded downstream of the ACS, with cumulative Mcm-ChEC signal peaking downstream and 77% (112/146) of CMBSs positioned downstream of their associated ACS within 100 base pairs, providing in vivo confirmation of in vitro predictions.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this directional loading finding. Reviewer 2 acknowledged 'the mobile nature of loaded Mcm2-7 double hexamers prevents any conclusions about the location of initial loading' but did not dispute the downstream positioning observation itself, treating it as a valid finding with appropriate caveats.

result: The most abundant 5500 CMBSs exhibit a pattern of GC skew characteristic of replication initiation, with a general rise in GC skew across CMBSs. GC-skew-based evidence for DNA replication initiation continued until approximately rank 6000, supporting the hypothesis that these sites have served as replication origins.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the GC skew analysis. Reviewer 1 stated the sites 'contain a G-C skew,' and Reviewer 2 noted 'a GC-skew centered around the site of Mcm loading,' affirming this characteristic as consistent with replication origins.

result: When Mcm is present, it exists predominantly as a single double hexamer across the entire abundance range, arguing against models where higher replication activity results from loading multiple Mcm double hexamers at individual origins within a single cell. Origin activity control operates through modulation of the fraction of cells with a double hexamer bound, rather than variation in the number of double hexamers per site.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge this mechanistic interpretation. Reviewer 2 noted 'the mobile nature of loaded Mcm2-7 double hexamers' as a caveat but did not dispute the single-hexamer observation or the population-level licensing model derived from it.

result: DNA replication origins are at least threefold more abundant than previously assumed, with multiple criteria converging on approximately 5500 total origins. Sites of replication initiation in yeast are much more widely dispersed than previously believed, with at least 1600 and possibly as many as 5500 origins.
evaluation: All reviewers affirmed this central conclusion. The editor stated the authors 'provide convincing evidence that the number of possible origins of replication is much higher than previously appreciated.' Reviewer 1 called the results 'convincing,' and Reviewer 2 stated the manuscript 'greatly broadens the number of sites that are capable of loading Mcm2-7.'

result: Replication may occasionally initiate in essentially every intergenic region, suggesting that with approximately 6000 genes in the yeast genome, replication can initiate, if only rarely, in essentially every intergenic region.
evaluation: This speculative extrapolation was not explicitly endorsed by reviewers. While reviewers accepted the broader distribution of origins, they did not specifically comment on the claim that every intergenic region could serve as an origin, leaving this more extreme interpretation without clear reviewer support.

result: The findings shed light on reports that 9-20% of replication events initiate outside known origins. The distribution of MCM abundance is consistent with single-molecule studies, with ~15% of replication initiation distributed among 5000 sites, explaining why these events appear unique in single-molecule studies.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this reconciliation with prior literature. Reviewer 1 noted the authors 'suggest, consistent with published single molecule results, that there are many more potential origins,' affirming the consistency with previous observations.

result: The broader distribution of replication origins suggests that S phase in yeast may be less distinct from that in humans than widely assumed.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this comparative interpretation. Reviewer 2 stated 'the ability to license and initiate replication from sites with increasing sequence divergence suggests a previously unappreciated versatility' and noted that 'these studies show that the sequence specificity of S. cerevisiae replication origins still sets it apart from metazoan origins' while acknowledging the reduced distinction.

result: Lower abundance intergenic MCM signals (ranks 500-4000) showed a distinct preference for divergent over convergent transcription of flanking genes, while the most abundant 500 sites showed a preference for convergent over divergent transcription.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these observations about transcriptional orientation preferences. The findings were presented as consistent with previous reports and were accepted as part of the characterization of origin features.

result: There was a short but obvious reversal in the GC skew trend precisely at the midpoint of Mcm binding sites, consistent with in vitro observations that Mcm single hexamers must cross over each other before diverging in bidirectional replication.
evaluation: Reviewers did not dispute this detailed GC skew pattern or its interpretation linking to biochemical findings. The observation was presented as consistent with established in vitro data and was implicitly accepted as part of the overall GC skew analysis.
